dominant_strengths: Familiar macOS Finder paradigm executed cleanly with traffic lights, sidebar groupings, and breadcrumb navigation feeling native and predictable.
Icon color coding (green code, pink PDF, blue images, purple fonts) creates quick categorical scanability across the grid.
dominant_weaknesses: Redundant breadcrumb shown twice — in toolbar and below — wasting vertical space and breaking information hierarchy without purpose.
Icon palette is loud and slightly cartoonish against an otherwise restrained chrome, creating tonal mismatch between content and frame.
Massive empty canvas below 18 items signals poor density planning; layout doesn't adapt or offer preview/metadata to justify the void.
fix_priorities: Remove duplicate breadcrumb row; consolidate into a single navigation strip.
Desaturate icon palette by ~20% so colors aid categorization without dominating the neutral shell.
Use vertical space for a metadata/preview pane or denser grid to eliminate dead area.
Tighten label typography — 'walkthrough.mov' wraps awkwardly while siblings sit on one line.
rationale.norman_balance: Behaviorally competent and native-feeling, but visceral charm is muted by clashing icon saturation and reflective payoff is low because nothing distinguishes it from default Finder.
rationale.intent_fit: It satisfies the file-browser brief functionally but offers no original perspective beyond a near-literal Finder reskin.
